messages.content: Hey, I just got out of the meeting with Boss Zhang about the Shenzhen trip. I was looking at tickets earlier and flight options for the trip are getting really expensive.
Yikes, last-minute flights will do that. Did you guys manage to sort out the budget situation despite the high prices?

Yeah, we talked through a few options. Someone actually suggested booking a cheaper hotel for the Shenzhen trip to save money. Boss Zhang just laughed and joked about the spicy food during the Shenzhen trip, saying we'd need a comfortable bathroom in a nicer hotel to survive it!
Haha, he makes a very valid point! So what did he end up deciding for the actual numbers?
He finally made the call. Boss Zhang decided that the budget cut for the Shenzhen trip is finalized at 12% instead of the 10% we talked about last week.
Got it, 12% it is. I'll make sure that final number is saved. Do you want me to help you look for flights that fit the new budget?
No, that's okay for now. I'll dig through the corporate portal myself in a bit to see what I can find.
Sounds good! Just give me a shout if you need a hand crunching the numbers later.

golden_memories: On 2025-08-25, Boss Zhang decided that the budget cut for the Shenzhen trip is finalized at 12% instead of 10%.

messages.content: Hey, I just talked to Jiange. He was joking around and asked if I was sweating yet about the in-laws visit.
Haha, he knows the pressure is on! Are you feeling the heat?
A bit! Especially since the mattress for the in-laws visit arrived yesterday, and it was surprisingly heavy. I could barely drag it into the apartment.
Those things are no joke! Are you going to need a hand getting it set up?
Yeah, definitely. Jiange scheduled to help me assemble the new guest bed for the in-laws visit at exactly 10:00 AM this Saturday.
That's a solid plan. I've noted down 10:00 AM this Saturday for the bed assembly with Jiange. Do you have all the tools you need?
Almost. Jiange recommended a good drill to use before the in-laws visit, so I'll probably run to the hardware store to buy it on Friday.
Perfect. I'll remind you to grab that drill on Friday. You'll have that guest room ready in no time!

golden_memories: On 2025-08-26, Jiange scheduled to help Linchen assemble the new guest bed for the in-laws visit at exactly 10:00 AM this Saturday.

messages.content: Hey, so Wanghao and I were just looking over the updated benchmark leaks for the Pixel 9 phone today. Turns out he concluded that the AI processing unit is actually exactly 25% faster than the previous generation, not 20% like we thought last week.
Oh, nice! A 25% bump is pretty solid, especially for on-device processing. Are you still planning to pre-order it for Liwei's birthday?

Yeah, definitely. Though Wanghao thought the new color options for the Pixel 9 phone were completely uninspired. I'm also wondering if a good case for the Pixel 9 phone will be hard to find right at launch.
Launch day cases can definitely be tricky to track down in stores. You might want to look for one online ahead of time. Any other concerns before you hit buy?

Just one thing. Wanghao and I debated whether the battery life of the Pixel 9 phone would actually last a full day with that faster AI chip running. We'll probably have to wait for real-world tests to know for sure.
That's a very valid point. More processing power usually means more battery drain. Keep an eye out for early reviews! Want me to set a reminder for the pre-order date?
Not yet, I'll let you know once the dates are officially announced. Thanks!
Sounds good! Just give me a shout when you're ready.

golden_memories: On 2025-08-27, Wanghao concluded that the AI processing unit on the Pixel 9 phone is exactly 25% faster than the previous generation based on new benchmarks.

messages.content: Hey, I really need to vent. I just felt a sudden wave of terror regarding the in-laws visit coming up. I was trying to cook, and I completely accidentally burned a practice batch of Mom's braised pork.
Oh no! Take a deep breath. That's exactly what practice batches are for—making the mistakes now instead of on the big day. Is the pot salvageable?
Barely, it's soaking now. I was chatting with Sister Chen about it, and she suggested buying pre-made sauce for the in-laws visit just to be safe. I'm starting to think she's right.
Sister Chen makes a good point! A high-quality pre-made sauce could take a ton of pressure off you. Are you going to take her advice?
I might have to. It's just frustrating because the grocery prices for the in-laws visit are really adding up, so ruining a whole batch of pork hurts my wallet too.
I hear you, wasting expensive ingredients is the worst. At least you caught the issue now. Have you figured out the rest of the prep for their arrival?
Getting there. Sister Chen and I also discussed what shirt I should wear on the first day of the in-laws visit, so I guess I have my wardrobe sorted, even if my cooking is a disaster.
Hey, looking sharp on day one is half the battle! Let the pot soak, get some rest, and we can look at backup sauce options tomorrow.

golden_memories: On 2025-08-28, Linchen felt a sudden wave of terror regarding the in-laws visit because he accidentally burned a practice batch of Mom's braised pork.

messages.content: Hey, I just got off the phone with Mom about Liwei's parents coming over for the in-laws visit.
How did the call go? Is she still giving you grief about burning that practice batch of braised pork yesterday?
Haha, a little bit. She also asked if the new apartment was fully dusted for the in-laws visit. I reminded her I already promised Liwei I'd deep clean the whole place.
Good thing you've already got that on your radar. Did she have any other pro-tips for hosting them?

Yeah, Mom advised serving green tea during the in-laws visit, so I'll need to buy some good quality leaves. Also, I checked the forecast and it looks like the weather for the in-laws visit will be sunny, which takes some pressure off.
Sunny weather and nice green tea sound like a very relaxing vibe. Are you feeling a bit less terrified now?
A bit! I just need to survive that initial meal. I actually promised Mom I would call her the moment the first dinner of the in-laws visit concludes so she knows if I ruined the pork again.
I can set a reminder for you to make that call right after dinner. You're going to do great, man!

golden_memories: On 2025-08-29, Linchen promised Mom he would call her the moment the first dinner of the in-laws visit concludes.

messages.content: Hey, I'm finally pulling the trigger on Liwei's birthday gift today. We were looking at the Pixel 9 phone again yesterday.
Nice! You've been planning that for a bit. Have you decided which version to get her?
Yeah, we talked about it a lot. She mentioned that the screen size of the Pixel 9 phone was perfect for watching videos. I did point out to her that the camera bump on it is quite large, though.
Yeah, that visor design is pretty prominent. Did the camera bump bother her at all?

Not really. We also read online that the shipping weight of the Pixel 9 phone box is very light, which is kind of random but good to know. Anyway, I made a serious commitment to her that I'll order the Pro model instead of the base model.
That's a fantastic gift! The Pro model's extra features will definitely make her day, especially since you promised. Want me to pull up the pre-order page?
No need, I've got the store page open right now and I'm checking out. Just wanted to get that sorted out before her parents visit next week.
Sounds good! You've got the phone sorted, now just the deep cleaning and the braised pork left to handle for the in-laws. Let me know if you need anything else!

golden_memories: On 2025-08-30, Linchen made a serious commitment to Liwei to order the Pro model of the Pixel 9 phone instead of the base model.

messages.content: Hey, could you update the plan for tonight? Jiange just texted me. His gym had a sudden closure, so he rescheduled the farewell dinner for the Shenzhen trip back to exactly 7:30 PM.
Got it! I've updated the farewell dinner to 7:30 PM. At least you won't have to wait around as long now. Everything else set?
Yeah, pretty much. Jiange wondered if we should order barbecue for the farewell dinner before the Shenzhen trip. I told him I'm totally down for that.
Barbecue sounds like the perfect pre-trip meal! Want me to look up the menu for you guys?
No need, we know the place well. We actually just talked about the restaurant's new decor for the dinner before the Shenzhen trip; apparently, they completely remodeled the interior.
Oh, that's cool! Good food and a fresh vibe. Are you all packed for tomorrow?
Almost done packing. I just really hope the traffic wouldn't be bad on the way to the airport for the Shenzhen trip tomorrow. I hate rushing to the gate.
Fingers crossed for smooth roads! I can check the traffic for you first thing in the morning. Have a great time at the dinner tonight!

messages.content: Hey, can you update the notes for the weekly sync? Boss Zhang changed things up again. During our chat, someone mentioned that reading the weekly sync memo on a phone is difficult.
Oh boy. I know he just capped it at two pages last Friday. What's the new plan to make it mobile-friendly?
Well, ironically, Boss Zhang suggested using a smaller font for the weekly sync memo so we wouldn't have to scroll as much.
A smaller font? That might make the phone reading issue even worse! How did you respond?
I tried to pivot. I asked if bullet points were preferred for the weekly sync instead of cramming in dense paragraphs.
Bullet points usually help with readability. Did he agree to that, or just give a hard limit on the content?
He didn't really care about the bullets, but he made a final call on the length. Boss Zhang decided that the written memo for the weekly sync must strictly not exceed one single page in length.
Understood. I've updated the constraints: the weekly sync memo is now strictly limited to one single page. I'll make sure to keep things ultra-concise when we draft it!

That sounds like a nightmare. How are you supposed to fit all those charts and metrics into just one page?
Exactly! I was practically pulling my hair out. Sister Chen saw me struggling and offered me an extra coffee just to help me survive writing this thing for the weekly sync.

Not really. We actually ended up joking that the weekly sync is turning into a poetry contest. Like, what's next, presenting our OKRs in haiku?
Data haikus... now that's a niche skill! At least you guys are finding some humor in the stress.
Yeah, we try. And to top it off, I just noticed the meeting room for the weekly sync is double-booked anyway. It's just a mess today.
Classic office logistics. Just do your best with the one-pager and let the room scheduling be someone else's headache!

Down to 30 seconds from 45! That's a solid improvement. And blue charts will definitely give the memo a fresh look.
